Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:21: The proof that the soul comprises two hundred forty-eight limbs is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Terumah 150a) and in several places: that the spirit [ruach] takes on a form in the lower Garden of Eden, clothed in the garment of the practical commandments, and takes on a likeness similar to what it had in this world; and he says (Zohar, Bereshit 7a) that in the lower Garden of Eden the righteous recognize one another - and this is (Psalms 31:20), "how great is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You, wrought for those who take refuge in You, before the sons of man" - and he says that the lower Garden of Eden is "before the sons of man" - for there they recognize one another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:22: Further, it is said in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 222b), in these words: "what is the reward for the soul in the World to Come? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, clothes it as before, in clouds of glory. At first it enters into a form [mareh] that is like the body, comprising two hundred forty-eight limbs; so too it enters into a 'mareh' comprising two hundred forty-eight commandments, and from the two hundred forty-eight lights that separate out from that form" - to this point. And it is explained afterward that six hundred thirteen angels raise up the soul, corresponding to the two hundred forty-eight positive and three hundred sixty-five negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:23: Since we now know that the portion of "ruach" comprises a complete stature of two hundred forty-eight limbs, so too the portion of "nefesh," which is in the courtyard [antechamber] of death, and the portion of "neshamah" that ascends to the upper Garden of Eden - each of them comprises two hundred forty-eight spiritual limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:24: With this introduction we may understand the matter of sin, which is fittingly called a "slain" [chalal] in the soul: just as an enemy who strikes a person's body with a sword is called "slain" [chalal], so too the sword of Samael, entering the two hundred forty-eight limbs of the soul, makes it "slain" and defiles it. The reason is: just as the impurity of a corpse comes about because the light of the holy soul has departed and the spirit of Samael's impurity rests there, defiling with a severe impurity - the corpse being the father of fathers of impurity - so too the sinner removes the holy soul from himself, and Samael rests in its place, and therefore he becomes defiled like a corpse. For this reason, the wicked, even in their lifetime, are called dead (Bereshit Rabbah 39:7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:25: To understand why it is called "slain" [chalal] and not "dead" regarding the soul - the matter is that a living person who is killed is called "chalal" because the vitality of the blood has departed from him, for the blood is the "nefesh," and the body remains "chalal," lifeless. And the term "chalal" is used as in (Exodus 31:14), "those who profane [mechaleleha] it shall surely be put to death" - which is explained in Parashat Bereshit (6a) concerning one who blemishes an inner point, so that that place remains "chalal" [hollow/empty]; and so too the matter of a sin that blemishes the essence of the soul, which is in the heart, makes it "chalal" there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:26: The general principle is that from the physical we understand the spiritual: any blow from which a person, if struck, would die and become "chalal" - so too a sin, according to its severity, in the limb of the soul it blemishes, is called "chalal" in the soul. And it is called "chalal" because the soul is holy, and sin is the turbidity of the spirit of impurity from Samael; and according to the extent that the spirit of impurity enters the soul, so its spirituality withdraws, and that place remains "chalal," without spirituality.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:27: This is the matter of the "blemish" [pegam] - for the word "pegam" means deficiency, that the light is lacking in that place and darkness from Samael rules there. Therefore, one who blemishes with his eyes darkens the eyes of his soul, and if, because of the severity of the blemish, he must come back in a transmigration [gilgul], he must be blind, and darkness and the clouds of Samael must rule over his eyes - as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (50a), in these words: "Samael is darkness, the serpent is gloom, and of it is said (Isaiah 50:3), 'I clothe the heavens with blackness' - its female counterpart - 'and sackcloth I make their covering.' Woe to the soul when it is clothed in their gloom, of which it is said (Genesis 27:1), 'and his eyes grew too dim to see' - these are the darknesses that cover the eyes, which have no permission to gaze upon the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah; and the light and lamp that shine within them are spoken of (Ecclesiastes 12:3), 'and those who look through the windows grow dim' - as Kohelet says (12:2), 'before the sun and the light grow dark,' and so on; and of the light and lamp it is said (Proverbs 6:23), 'for the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light.' And why do they grow dark in them? Because they do not occupy themselves with Torah and commandment in the fear and love that are Yud-Heh; and as soon as they occupy themselves with them in fear and love, an oath is sworn by the Holy One, blessed be He, to remove them [the darknesses] from the world, and the soul - because of the darknesses - separates between Yud-Heh and Vav-Heh. And at the time when the darknesses are removed from the soul, immediately 'let every soul praise Yah.' And who are these darknesses? Samael and the serpent. And who causes them to rule? Rather, the secret of the verse teaches (Isaiah 59:2), 'but your iniquities have separated between you and your God.' And David, concerning them, said (Psalms 119:18), 'open my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things from Your Torah' - at that time, what darknesses ruled over the lights of the eyes is reversed, and the lights rule over the darknesses" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:28: It is explained in this passage that Samael and the serpent are the darknesses that darken the eyes, and this is because of sin, as it says, "for your iniquities have separated," and so on; and incidentally it is explained in the passage that the cause of the darkening of the eyes is also because they do not occupy themselves with Torah and commandment in fear and love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:29: Let us return to our discourse: every blemish a person causes is a blemish in the soul and darkens its light, and for this reason sin is called "chalal" in the soul, for the reason explained. Now, according to this, we may say that every single sin a person blemishes with is called "chalal" - the intent being either a minor death or a greater death, all called "death," in the sense that "a poor person is considered as dead," and others our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Nedarim 64b), that the cause of the withdrawal of one's flow and light is called "death"; so too, regarding "chalal," any withdrawal of the light of the soul because of sin, leaving that place "chalal" for Samael to enter, is called "chalal" in the soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:30: Now that it is explained that sin is what darkens the soul, we may understand what our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, cited in the Yalkut (Psalms, Psalm 68, remez 795), on the verse (Psalms 68:12), "the LORD gives the word": it was taught by Rashbi: before the first man sinned, he would hear the Voice and stand on his feet, as it is said (Genesis 3:8), "and they heard the voice of the LORD God"; but once he sinned, he would hear it and hide, as it is said, "and the man hid himself." Before Israel sinned, what is written (Exodus 24:17)? "And the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire." Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: seven walls of fire were sparkling one within another, and Israel saw and were neither afraid nor terrified; but once they sinned, they could not even look upon the face of the intermediary [Moses] - this is [the meaning of] (Exodus 34:30), "and Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and behold, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:31: The reason for this is that when the soul is clear and bright, it can gaze upon light - like one standing in light, whom the sunlight does not harm; but one standing in darkness, if sunlight strikes his eyes, cannot bear it and recoils, turning back and covering his eyes. So too Israel: at the giving of the Torah, the impurity of their sin ceased and their soul was refined through the counting of seven weeks for their purification, and three days before receiving the Torah they were warned not to approach a woman, as it is said (Exodus 19:15), "be ready for the third day; do not approach a woman," and they washed their garments through immersion - all these good preparations to refine their soul to receive the Torah, and through this they were able to gaze [upon the light]. But once they sinned, they returned to draw upon themselves the impurity and darkness of the serpent, and darkened their soul, until they could not even look upon the face of the intermediary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:1: One must fear lest his soul be cast outward when it ascends above at its departure from this world, as Rashbi explains (Zohar, Pinchas 213b), on the verse (Psalms 86:2), "guard my soul, for I am pious [chasid]" - in these words: "'guard my soul' - it should have said 'shemor' [guard, masculine form]! And we have learned that there is not a single letter in the Torah that does not contain supernal and precious secrets. 'Shomrah' [guard it] - this is said to the Holy One, blessed be He, concerning that portion with which my soul is united; for when the soul departs from this world, it comes to inherit [its] world - if it merits, how many supernal hosts go forth to receive it and guard it and bring it into the dwelling of its place! And this Heh guards it, to be united with it at the New Moons and Sabbaths. But if it does not merit, how many wardens of impure spirits are assembled to receive it, and they push it outward! Woe to that soul that is tossed about, empty, like a stone in a sling - this is [the meaning of] (I Samuel 25:29), 'and the souls of your enemies, He shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling.' And David made his plea before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said, 'guard my soul,' that they should not push it outward, and when it comes to receive it, may they open gates for it and receive it before You" - to this point. Now, if King David, peace be upon him, needed to pray that his soul not be cast outward, how much more must one who is full of countless sins fear his sins, and hasten to repentance and prayer, before the day comes when regret will no longer help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:2: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 3b): Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said, in the name of Rabbi Yonatan: whoever performs a single commandment in this world, it precedes him and goes before him into the World to Come, as it is said (Isaiah 58:8), "and your righteousness shall go before you." And whoever commits a transgression in this world, it wraps around him and goes before him to the Day of Judgment, as it is said (Job 6:18), "the paths of their way turn aside; they go up into the void and are lost." Rabbi Elazar says: it is bound to him like a dog, as it is said (Genesis 39:10), "and he did not listen to her, to lie beside her, to be with her" - "to lie beside her" in this world, "to be with her" in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:3: The matter of "it wraps around him and goes before him to the Day of Judgment" is because whoever commits a single transgression acquires for himself a single accuser, and each and every accuser has the measure of a complete stature - just as with a commandment, so with a transgression. Behold, there are two hundred forty-eight commandments, the stature of the supernal Adam, two hundred forty-eight holy limbs; and every commandment contains an allusion to "the LORD," as is explained in the Tikkunim (73a, 131b) and Ra'aya Meheimna (see Pinchas 228b), that a commandment is [an anagram of, or has the letters of] "the LORD" [reading the Aramaic "mitzvah" as containing an allusion]; and "the LORD" is the totality of the whole stature, except that within each and every limb is the totality of everything. Therefore, one who fulfills a single commandment properly is as though he fulfilled them all, as I explained above in chapter four in the name of Rashbi, peace be upon him - and from it is made a single complete angel, with two hundred forty-eight limbs, who is his defender.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:4: Similar to this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 12) concerning the first man, that he contained the totality of all souls - some hang from the hairs of his head, some from his arm, some from his body, some from his legs, and so on. And just as every soul comprises two hundred forty-eight limbs, yet is nevertheless the portion of a particular limb, so too every accuser, since it is made from the power of this person through the power of all his two hundred forty-eight limbs, has two hundred forty-eight limbs, and is the portion of a particular limb of the stature of Samael.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:5: This is [the meaning of] "do not say, I will repay evil" (Proverbs 20:22), which is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Miketz (201a), that you should not say, I will complete the evil - which is Samael - through my sins, to give him a complete stature; and it says that this loathsome one is completed only through the sins of mankind, and therefore a person must be careful not to let that evil inclination be completed through his sins, and should always be on guard - for the good inclination seeks always to complete itself in perfection, not the evil inclination. Therefore, "do not say, I will repay evil; wait for the LORD, and He will save you" - to this point. We find, then, that the full stature [of the evil forces] is completed through many evil deeds, but each and every sin, and each portion-limb of it, comprises two hundred forty-eight, as I have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:6: With this introduction we may understand "it wraps around him and goes before him to the Day of Judgment" - meaning that it wraps around him entirely and becomes a garment for his soul, to bring him into Gehinnom, until that ugliness and darkness in the soul is consumed. This is the matter of the "filthy garments" that Rashbi explains (Pinchas 214a) are put upon the soul to bring it into Gehinnom, in these words: "Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Zechariah 3:1), 'and he showed me Yehoshua the High Priest, standing before the angel of the LORD,' and so on. Come and see, woe to those people who do not gaze upon the glory of their Master, and every single day a herald calls out concerning them, and they pay no heed! [If] a person comes to gaze upon the commandments of the Torah, how many defenders stand to speak well of him! [If] a person comes and transgresses the commandments of the Torah, they become accusers against him, speaking ill of him before the Holy One, blessed be He. Yehoshua was a High Priest, as has been established; what is written of him? 'And Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him.' And if this was so for him, how much more so for the rest of the people of the world who do not gaze upon their Master!
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:7: See what is written of him: "and Yehoshua was clothed in filthy garments," as has been established. But the filthy garments are certainly the garments in which the spirit is clothed in that world; and it has been said that whoever is to enter Gehinnom, what are the garments they clothe him in? What is written here? "And Yehoshua was clothed in filthy garments, and stood before the angel." Which angel is this? The angel appointed over Gehinnom, appointed over whoever is seen in those garments - until he answered and said, "remove the filthy garments from upon him." From here we may derive that a person's deeds make for him these filthy garments; and it says to him, "see, I have removed your iniquity from upon you, and I will clothe you with fine robes" - He clothes him with other, proper garments, through which a person may gaze upon the splendor of his Master's glory" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:8: It is explained that a person's deeds are what make these filthy garments for him - according to the number of his sins, so the number of garments, for each and every sin makes a garment for him; and this is "it wraps around him," stated in the passage. And the proof of this is "see, I have removed your iniquity from upon you," which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (see Targum Zechariah) refers to the iniquity that his sons had married foreign women.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:9: Rabbi Elazar said: it is bound to him like a dog - meaning that it not only makes a garment for him, but cleaves to the soul itself, to be attached to it; and it is the way of a biting dog that a portion of the person is found within its teeth, and it is the way of one bitten by a dog to see [visions of] dogs before him, even within his urine, as is observed by experience many times. We find, then, a portion of the transgression within the soul itself, and this is the matter of the blemish I explained, which is "chalal" in the soul; and further, a portion of the soul remains within the transgression, which is the power of Lilith - and this is the matter of "bound," a double bond, this within that and that within this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:10: The portion of the transgression that becomes acquired in his soul is what accompanies him in this world, and this is "to lie beside her in this world." And the portion of his soul that remains within it [the transgression] is "to be with her in the World to Come" - for Lilith seizes hold of him because of that portion which remains within her, to bring him down to Gehinnom. And we find that this particular detail of blemish, lying with a gentile woman, is alluded to in this verse mentioned in the story of Joseph; and the reason is that through his lying with her, he casts a spirit into her, which is a portion of his soul, and therefore he is compelled to be with her in the World to Come - and this is "bound like a dog," as will be explained, with God's help, concerning the matter of the "dog."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:11: However, we may say that with every single transgression by which a person defiles himself through that evil desire, he lies with Lilith - for all the desires of the world are from the power of Lilith, since Samael, because of his extreme subtlety, has no connection by which to take hold of man, who is physical; therefore he sends his female counterpart, who is more physical, and she is the seductress. And likewise, concerning the seven chambers of impurity, which correspond to Lilith, it is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (262b-268a), that from them spread forth many enticements for the children of man, and many pleasures in this world, and she shows him many faces to cause him to sin and to draw him to her. We find, then, that in following the affairs of this world, a person is drawn after her, and his soul is bound to him like a dog. And the first man, because he followed the enticements of the serpent, which are the powers of Lilith, caused death for himself and for those who came after him, as is explained in Parashat Pekudei, at the beginning of the chambers of impurity (262b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:12: It is explained in Parashat Vayetze, in the Tosefta (148a), that Lilith is the seductress, while Samael does not seduce because of his subtlety, in these words: "the secret of secrets: from within the strength of the midday brightness of Isaac, from within the dregs of wine, came forth a single hardened knot, comprising both male and female, red as a rose, dividing into several sides and paths. The male is called Samael; his female counterpart is comprised within him always - just as it is on the holy side, so too on the other side, male and female comprised one within the other. Samael's female is called the serpent, a woman of harlotries, the end of all flesh, the end of days. Two evil spirits cleave together as one: the spirit of the male is subtle; the spirit of the female divides into several ways and paths, and cleaves to that spirit of the male. She adorns herself with many ornaments like a distant harlot; she stands at the head of the ways and paths to seduce the children of man. The fool who draws near her, she seizes him and kisses him, and gives him to drink wine mixed with the dregs of the venom of vipers; once he has drunk, he strays after her. After she has seen him stray after her from the path of truth, she strips herself of all those adornments with which she was adorned for that fool.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:13: Her adornments to seduce the children of man: her hair is arranged, red as a rose; her face is white and red; in her ears hang six ornaments, [from] the treasury of Egypt; hanging upon her neck are all the finery of the ancient land; her mouth is arranged with a small, fine opening, beautiful in its adornment; her tongue is sharp as a sword; her words are smooth as oil; her lips are lovely, red as a rose, sweetened with all the sweetness of the world; she is clothed in purple, adorned with thirty-nine adornments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:14: The fool who strays after her drinks from the cup of wine, commits adultery with her, and strays after her. What does she do? She leaves him asleep in bed and ascends above and slanders him, and receives permission and descends. That fool awakens and thinks to make merry with her as before, but she has removed her adornments from herself and turned into a mighty warrior standing opposite him, clothed in a garment of flaming fire, with fierce dread, making his body and soul tremble - naked, full of eyes of terror, a sharpened sword in her hand, from which bitter drops hang. She kills that fool and casts him into Gehinnom" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:15: All these are parables - just as King Solomon, peace be upon him, likened the affairs of the world and its pleasures, which flow from the power of Lilith, to a harlot woman, as it is said (Proverbs 7:10), "and behold, a woman comes to meet him, dressed as a harlot, wily of heart," and so on - as her words and counsels are explained in Parashat Pekudei, in the chambers of impurity (267a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:16: It is explained in the passage we cited, "the spirit of the male is subtle," and so on, "the spirit of the female divides into several paths," and so on - we see that the female spreads out, and all this is a pattern of the supernal realm, for "one corresponding to the other God has made": just as above, the male does not act at all, but everything is effected through the female, so too below, in the impure powers. And just as above she acts only through the power of the male, so too below - and this is [the meaning of] "and cleaves to that spirit of the male."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:17: It remains for us to explain a point in this passage: why is the transgression likened to a dog, and not to a serpent or something else? The matter may be understood from what is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 224b): that just as with sacrifices, if they [Israel] merited, the image of a fiery lion would descend, crouching upon the altar, and if not, a dog - so too at the departure of the soul, in these words: "as our Rabbis established, if they merited, a fiery lion would descend to consume the sacrifices; if not, a fiery dog would descend there. So too, when a person dies: if he merits, [an angel] in the image of a lion descends to receive his soul; if not, in the image of a dog - of which David said (Psalms 22:21), 'deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:18: To know the reason for the lion and the dog, know that it is explained in Parashat Bereshit (6b) that the angel in the image of a lion that would descend upon the altar was named Uriel, and so it is explained in Parashat Tzav (32b). And my teacher explained that the reason for its being in the image of a lion is that its nourishment is from the right, as it is said (Ezekiel 1:10), "and the face of a lion was to the right for all four of them," and so on. Nevertheless, we must know why it was specifically Uriel who would descend, and it appears that the reason is what Rashbi explains in the sixth chamber of the holy chambers (254b) concerning Raphael and Uriel - he explains there that Raphael is in Tiferet, from where healing and life flow downward, and Uriel is in Malchut.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:19: Now, in Parashat Bereshit (51a), on the verse (Deuteronomy 4:24), "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire" - it is explained that the fire of the Shechinah, which is a consuming fire, would consume the sacrifices, in these words: "and this is the secret of the sacrifice: the smoke that ascends arouses this blue-black light to be kindled, and when it is kindled it joins with the white light, and the lamp burns in a single unity. And because the way of this blue-black light is to destroy and to consume all that cleaves to it beneath it, when [divine] favor is present and the lamp burns in a single union, then it is written, 'and fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering,' and so on; and then it becomes known that that lamp burns in a single union," and so on - to the extent relevant here. Behold, the descent of the fire came from the Shechinah, through the illumination of Tiferet within her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:20: And it says afterward: after the supernal fire finished consuming the sacrifice, what did the supernal fire [continue to] consume? And it says that Israel would cleave through arousal from below - priests, Levites, and Israelites: these through the joy of song, these through the desire of the heart, and these through prayer - and the lamp would burn, and the lights would cleave together as one. We find, then, that the fire of Uriel, which would descend upon the altar, necessarily came about through the Shechinah's clothing herself in it through the illumination of Tiferet - and this is the name of the angel Uriel, explained in Parashat Pekudei (254b), as being within the Shechinah, comprising all of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:21: Now, concerning the departure of the righteous one's soul from this world, Rashbi explains (Vayechi 235a), on the verse (Proverbs 5:15), "drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well" - that then the union [of male and female] takes place, and the soul becomes, within it, "female waters" [mayin nukvin] - see there. If so, it is necessarily the angel Uriel, who corresponds to her [the Shechinah], who must descend to raise up the righteous one's soul, which is from the power of the male, so that through his good deeds it is aroused to union, similar to what happened with the sacrifice.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:22: Regarding the matter of the dog, it is explained there, in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar 6b): if they did not merit, a dog would descend, and the name of that dog is "Bil'adan" - for he is not included among mankind [Adam], but is a dog, with the face of a dog.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:23: Know that this too is "one corresponding to the other God has made": just as Uriel corresponds to the Shechinah, for the arousal of good, so Bil'adan, the face of a dog, corresponds to the arousal of evil deeds. And undoubtedly the sacrifice was given to the dog only when it was disqualified, and therefore "you shall cast it to the dog" [Exodus 22:30], as is explained in the Tikkunim (33b, 62b) concerning a disqualified prayer that is given over to the dog. This dog corresponds to Lilith, and therefore its name is "Bil'adan" - meaning that it denies the providence of the Shechinah, who is called "Adonai" [my Lord] - "Bil'adan" meaning "he has no lord" [bli adon]. And so the Geonim explained that the names of the ten kelipot mostly indicate a denial of Godhood, as my teacher, peace be upon him, cited their words in Sefer HaPardes, Gate of Substitutions; and this is the insolence of dogs, who are called "brazen of soul" (Isaiah 56:11). And with this we may offer another explanation of "Uriel" - meaning one who acknowledges the providence of God [El] over him - this being "Uriel," "the light I have is from God" - the secret of "and God is indignant [with the wicked]" (Psalms 7:12), as is explained in Parashat Bamidbar (Zohar 30b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:24: There is further proof, in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Naso 124a), that the "dog" is among the powers of Lilith, in these words: "the evil inclination, from the right side, is called the serpent; and from the left side, that of Esau, whose grade is Samael, it is called a dog, the appointed one of Gehinnom, who cries 'give, give' - this is [the meaning of] (Proverbs 30:15), 'the leech has two daughters: give, give.' Its desire is to consume the defiled soul in its fire, Gehinnom; and a spirit of jealousy passes over it and it is jealous of its wife, in truth, and she has been defiled - and concerning her it is said (Leviticus 21:9), 'and the daughter of a priest' - this is Michael - 'if she begins to profane herself by harlotry, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.' And there that filth is burned, and that portion is refined like silver refined in fire, and that dross-lead-filth is burned and becomes dust and is crushed" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:25: Behold, it says that the evil inclination, which is from the power of Lilith, as I explained above, that the enticements of the evil inclination are from the side of Lilith - from the right side it is called "serpent," and from the left side it is called "dog." And it says that this dog is the appointed one of Gehinnom, who cries "give, give"; and it is already known that the entire reality of Gehinnom and its seven chambers are from the powers of "the strange, foreign woman," as is explained in Parashat Pekudei.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:26: As for what it says, that from the right side it is called "serpent" - we find that the serpent seduced the first man and Eve, and that seduction proceeded from his right side, "for God knows that on the day you eat of it... you shall be like gods," and so on (Genesis 3:5); and similarly with the rest of the enticements of the evil inclination, all of which come from the right side, which draws near, to show him peace, tranquility, and security - "eat and drink," and the like of the good things of this world that flow from the right. And afterward it is called "dog," which cries out against him to cast him into Gehinnom, in the manner explained in the passage from Parashat Vayetze cited above - and this is [the pattern of] "it descends and incites, it ascends and accuses, it descends and takes the soul" (see Bava Batra 16a and Ein Yaakov there).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:27: Because this dog corresponds to Lilith, King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 22:21), "deliver my soul from the sword" - this being the sword of Lilith, as explained in the passage from Parashat Vayetze (148a); "from the power of the dog, my only one" - referring to the soul that ascends to union, as explained in Parashat Vayechi (235a), and therefore called "my only one" [yechidati], from the language of "yichud" [union]. "Deliver" - that the dog should not seize it, this being the one who seizes the soul when it has a disqualification, as explained in the passage from Parashat Vayetze - that Lilith is the one who seduces him with the affairs of the world and defiles him, and she kills him and casts him into Gehinnom. And do not wonder that "dog" is masculine [in that passage] though [Lilith is female] - for from the side of Samael-Esau it is called "dog" from the left side, as is explained in the passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:28: Because most sins come from the enticements of Lilith, as I have explained, and she is called "dog" in the manner explained, therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yoma 86b): one who sins and repeats [the sin] is like a dog that returns to its vomit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 8:29: Therefore a person must guard himself against these powers of wickedness and their enticements, for their entire intent is to trip a person up and catch him in their net, and cast him into a roaring pit, into the mire of the depths, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, elaborated in the chambers of impurity (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei) - see there. For by a person's knowledge of the punishments for these matters, he will guard himself from them, and may God help him.
